articles.title: SJAA Swap Meet October 29, 2017
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held its annual Fall Swap Meet on October 29, 2017, at Houge Park Hall. The event was well-attended by buyers, including members from other Bay Area clubs, and successfully raised over $2,000, largely from donated equipment. A large 24" Dobsonian telescope donated to the club is still available for purchase.

articles.title: Stargazing party at the Pinnacles, a huge hit
articles.summary: A stargazing party at Pinnacles National Park on September 16, 2017, drew approximately 200 participants who enjoyed viewing celestial objects like Saturn, Neptune, and various nebulae through ten telescopes provided by astronomers. The event, highlighted by its clear dark skies away from city light pollution, served as a successful public outreach effort promoting dark sky conservation. Attendees, including many from surrounding cities, expressed awe at the visible wonders and the knowledge shared by the astronomers.

articles.title: San Jose Tech Museum Star Party
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a successful star party on the San Jose Tech Museum roof for attendees of the Association of Science Technology Centers (ASTC) convention. Ten SJAA telescopes, supplemented by four from the Eastbay Astronomical Society, provided views of celestial objects like Saturn, globular clusters (M2, M11, M13), the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), and the Pleiades (M45) to nearly 2,000 science museum professionals. The event was a great nighttime experience, fostering curiosity and appreciation for astronomy among a science-oriented audience.

articles.title: O'Neil Total Solar Eclipse Adventure
articles.summary: Bill O'Neil recounts his family's successful adventure to observe and photograph the August 21, 2017 Total Solar Eclipse from Mitchell, Oregon. They meticulously planned their trip a year in advance, securing lodging and visiting local attractions, including a Native American museum and the Painted Hills. Using specialized equipment and "Solar Eclipse Maestro" software, they captured stunning images of the eclipse phases, culminating in a celebratory "Corona" beer toast.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Posts
articles.summary: This article compiles diverse observation reports from members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It details experiences from the 2017 Total Solar Eclipse in Oregon, reviews of multi-day star parties like Calstar and West Pinnacles, and an exciting solar prominence and flare event. Additionally, members report on an equipment upgrade project for accessory cases and the scouting of new dark sky observing locations.

articles.title: Hubble's Messier Catalog
articles.summary: The article details Charles Messier's life and the creation of his famous catalog of deep-sky objects, initially intended to help comet hunters avoid non-cometary targets. It explains how the 110-object Messier Catalog became popular among amateur astronomers and highlights the contributions of the Hubble Space Telescope, which has observed 93 Messier objects, using various wavelengths to provide scientific insights despite its narrow field of view. These observations deepen understanding for all astronomy enthusiasts, from professional researchers to amateur observers.

articles.title: 95 Minutes Over Jupiter
articles.summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft captured a 95-minute sequence of 11 color-enhanced images during its Perijove 8 flyby of Jupiter on September 1, 2017. Taken by JunoCam, these images dramatically illustrate the rapid change in viewing geometry as the spacecraft traveled from Jupiter's north pole to its south pole. The sequence highlights various features, including the polar regions and a mid-southern latitude blue vortex, some identified as public 'Points of Interest,' with raw images made available for citizen science processing.

articles.title: More Than 2.4 Million Names Are Going to Mars
articles.summary: NASA successfully gathered over 2.4 million names from the public to be etched on microchips and sent to Mars aboard the InSight mission. This initiative, which invited participation in 2015 and again in late 2017, allowed space enthusiasts to contribute to the upcoming May 2018 launch. The InSight lander will be the first mission to study Mars' deep interior by listening for marsquakes, providing crucial insights into the formation of rocky planets.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: The article showcases an astrophotography gallery featuring deep-sky images captured by members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), including nebulae and galaxies. Each photograph is accompanied by detailed technical specifications, outlining the equipment used, filters, exposure times, and post-processing software. This collection highlights the members' skills and methodologies in capturing celestial objects from various California locations.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: The "Kid Spot" article presents astronomy-themed content for a younger audience, featuring space-related jokes and a quiz on telescope basics. It also includes historical excerpts from a September 2016 Astronomy Magazine edition, highlighting key astronomical discoveries and events from 1930 to 1938, such as the discovery of Pluto, the birth of radio astronomy, and the proposal of dark matter.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) board meetings in late 2017 addressed several key administrative and operational items. These included updates on the Hogue Park application, renewals for the Mendoza Ranch permit and Calstar insurance rider, and the approval of the 2018 calendar. Discussions also covered partnerships with the Open Space Authority for "Starry Nights" events, planning for the Swap Meet, the future of the Ephemeris publication, and clarifying the purpose and funding for a "JVN Thank You Scope."

articles.title: Amending Bylaws: Memberships
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) board amended its bylaws in July 2017, removing the option for youth or student memberships and restricting membership to individuals aged 18 and above. This decision was made due to the historically low number of minor members and new, burdensome City of San Jose requirements for volunteers who have "direct contact" with minors. By solidifying that SJAA volunteers only have incidental contact with minors, the organization aims to avoid onerous background check requirements and ensure the continued viability of its public events.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a diverse range of programs and resources for its members and the community. These include a library, free telescope repair sessions, regular solar and night sky observing events, and beginner-friendly "Quick STARt" and "Intro to the Night Sky" programs. Additionally, SJAA provides an equipment loaner program and specialized groups and workshops for astro-imaging enthusiasts, catering to all ages and experience levels in amateur astronomy.
